flags.headline: FTNT new AMBER — 'FortiBleed' credential-exposure campaign hits ~86,600 FortiGate devices
flags.detail: First flagged this run (event itself dates to mid-to-late June and was not previously captured by the Sentinel). CISA issued an emergency alert on 2026-06-18 after leaked administrator credentials for an initial ~74,000 Fortinet firewalls/VPN gateways were found in active use by threat actors; the confirmed count has since grown to ~86,644 unique FortiGate devices across 194 countries — roughly half of internet-facing Fortinet firewalls. A Russian-speaking threat group reportedly ran ~1.16B credential attempts against 320,000+ FortiGate targets; compromised admin credentials allow firewall-rule tampering, VPN interception, backdoor accounts, and ransomware staging. This does not match a listed key_risk verbatim (FTNT's screener report risks are valuation, platform competition, and org-scalability), but a security vendor's own appliances being the vector is a trust/reputational risk worth the desk's attention. Not yet visible in price (FTNT -1.76%, in line with the broader sector move, not an outlier) or in analyst recommendation counts (unchanged month-over-month in the data drop).
